claim: Physical activity has been associated with preventing the development of type 2 diabetes and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.
source: Physical activity has been associated with preventing the development of type 2 diabetes and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.
evidence: This is a well-established scientific consensus supported by the citation to Piercy et al., 2018.

claim: Both acute- and long-term exercise may enhance insulin sensitivity and thereby improve glucose tolerance.
source: Both acute- and long-term exercise may enhance insulin sensitivity and thereby improve glucose tolerance (Hawley and Lessard, 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to Hawley and Lessard, 2008.

claim: Both resistance and endurance exercises enhance insulin sensitivity, although the most pronounced effect is observed when combining these training modalities.
source: Both resistance and endurance exercises enhance insulin sensitivity, although the most pronounced effect is observed when combining these training modalities (Bacchi et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Bacchi et al., 2012.

claim: Exerkines are molecules secreted from various tissues in response to acute- and/or long-term exercise with endocrine, paracrine, and/or autocrine functions.
source: These exerkines are secreted from various tissues and include a variety of signal molecules released in response to acute- and/or long-term exercise with endocrine, paracrine, and/or autocrine functions (Pedersen et al., 2007; Chow et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citations to Pedersen et al., 2007 and Chow et al., 2022.

claim: Interleukin-6 (IL6) is released during muscle contractions and contributes to improved overall glucose homeostasis.
source: The established bona fide exerkine, interleukin-6 (IL6), is released during muscle contractions, contributing to improved overall glucose homeostasis (Pedersen et al., 2007; Kistner et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citations to Pedersen et al., 2007 and Kistner et al., 2022.

claim: The MyoGlu study analyzed 3072 serum proteins in 26 men undergoing 12 weeks of combined strength and endurance exercise intervention.
source: We analyzed 3072 serum proteins in 26 men, normal weight or overweight, undergoing 12 weeks of a combined strength and endurance exercise intervention.
evidence: This is a direct description of the study design and methods.

claim: Following 12 weeks of exercise intervention, 283 serum proteins showed significant changes.
source: Following 12 weeks of exercise intervention, we observed significant changes in 283 serum proteins.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study's proteomic analysis.

claim: 66 proteins were elevated in overweight men and positively associated with liver fat before the exercise regimen, but were normalized after exercise.
source: Notably, 66 of these proteins were elevated in overweight men and positively associated with liver fat before the exercise regimen, but were normalized after exercise.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study's analysis of protein changes in overweight men.

claim: For 19.7% of the exercise-responsive proteins, corresponding changes in mRNA expression levels in muscle were shown.
source: Furthermore, for 19.7 and 12.1% of the exercise-responsive proteins, corresponding changes in mRNA expression levels in muscle and fat, respectively, were shown.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the multi-omic analysis.

claim: For 12.1% of the exercise-responsive proteins, corresponding changes in mRNA expression levels in fat were shown.
source: Furthermore, for 19.7 and 12.1% of the exercise-responsive proteins, corresponding changes in mRNA expression levels in muscle and fat, respectively, were shown.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the multi-omic analysis.

claim: The protein CD300LG displayed consistent alterations in blood, muscle, and fat.
source: The protein CD300LG displayed consistent alterations in blood, muscle, and fat.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the multi-tissue analysis.

claim: Serum CD300LG exhibited positive associations with insulin sensitivity.
source: Serum CD300LG exhibited positive associations with insulin sensitivity, and to angiogenesis-related gene expression in both muscle and fat.
evidence: This is a finding from the correlation analysis in the MyoGlu study.

claim: Serum CD300LG was positively associated with physical activity in the UK Biobank.
source: Furthermore, serum CD300LG was positively associated with physical activity and negatively associated with glucose levels in the UK Biobank.
evidence: This is a finding from the UK Biobank analysis.

claim: Serum CD300LG was negatively associated with glucose levels in the UK Biobank.
source: Furthermore, serum CD300LG was positively associated with physical activity and negatively associated with glucose levels in the UK Biobank.
evidence: This is a finding from the UK Biobank analysis.

claim: The association between serum CD300LG and physical activity was significantly stronger in men than in women.
source: In this sample, the association between serum CD300LG and physical activity was significantly stronger in men than in women.
evidence: This is a finding from the sex-stratified analysis in the UK Biobank.

claim: Mendelian randomization analysis suggested potential causal relationships between levels of serum CD300LG and fasting glucose.
source: Mendelian randomization analysis suggested potential causal relationships between levels of serum CD300LG and fasting glucose, 2 hr glucose after an oral glucose tolerance test, and HbA1c.
evidence: This is a finding from the Mendelian randomization analysis.

claim: Mendelian randomization analysis suggested potential causal relationships between levels of serum CD300LG and 2 hr glucose after an oral glucose tolerance test.
source: Mendelian randomization analysis suggested potential causal relationships between levels of serum CD300LG and fasting glucose, 2 hr glucose after an oral glucose tolerance test, and HbA1c.
evidence: This is a finding from the Mendelian randomization analysis.

claim: Mendelian randomization analysis suggested potential causal relationships between levels of serum CD300LG and HbA1c.
source: Mendelian randomization analysis suggested potential causal relationships between levels of serum CD300LG and fasting glucose, 2 hr glucose after an oral glucose tolerance test, and HbA1c.
evidence: This is a finding from the Mendelian randomization analysis.

claim: Cd300lg responded to exercise in a mouse model.
source: Additionally, Cd300lg responded to exercise in a mouse model, and we observed signs of impaired glucose tolerance in male, but not female, Cd300lg knockout mice.
evidence: This is a finding from the mouse exercise model analysis.

claim: Male, but not female, Cd300lg knockout mice showed signs of impaired glucose tolerance.
source: Additionally, Cd300lg responded to exercise in a mouse model, and we observed signs of impaired glucose tolerance in male, but not female, Cd300lg knockout mice.
evidence: This is a finding from the Cd300lg knockout mouse model.

claim: The MyoGlu study enrolled 26 men aged 40–65 years who were healthy but sedentary.
source: The MyoGlu study enrolled men aged 40–65 years who were healthy but sedentary (having engaged in fewer than one exercise session per week in the previous year) (Langleite et al., 2016; Lee et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a description of the study cohort.

claim: Participants in the MyoGlu study were divided into two groups: overweight (with an average BMI of 29.5 ± 2.3 kg/m2) and normal weight controls (with an average BMI of 23.6 ± 2.0 kg/m2).
source: These participants were divided into two groups based on their body mass index (BMI) and glucose tolerance: overweight (with an average BMI of 29.5 ± 2.3 kg/m2) and normal weight controls (with an average BMI of 23.6 ± 2.0 kg/m2).
evidence: This is a description of the study groups with specific BMI values.

claim: The overweight men had reduced glucose tolerance and/or insulin sensitivity.
source: The overweight men had reduced glucose tolerance and/or insulin sensitivity (Supplementary file 1A).
evidence: This is a baseline characteristic of the overweight group.

claim: The 12-week training intervention included two weekly sessions of 60 min each for endurance cycling and two sessions of 60 min each for whole-body strength training.
source: This 12-week training intervention included two weekly sessions of 60 min each for endurance cycling and two sessions of 60 min each for whole-body strength training.
evidence: This is a description of the exercise intervention protocol.

claim: After the 12-week intervention, body fat mass decreased and lean body mass increased in both groups.
source: After the 12-week intervention, body fat mass decreased and lean body mass increased, together with significant improvements in insulin sensitivity (~40%), maximum oxygen uptake and muscle strength in both groups (Supplementary file 1A).
evidence: This is a primary outcome of the intervention study.

claim: After the 12-week intervention, insulin sensitivity improved by approximately 40% in both groups.
source: After the 12-week intervention, body fat mass decreased and lean body mass increased, together with significant improvements in insulin sensitivity (~40%), maximum oxygen uptake and muscle strength in both groups (Supplementary file 1A).
evidence: This is a primary outcome of the intervention study.

claim: 126 proteins increased in serum concentration following the 12-week intervention at an FDR below 5%.
source: Of the 3072 proteins quantified, we detected increased serum concentrations of 126 proteins and decreased serum concentrations of 157 proteins following the 12-week intervention at an FDR below 5% (Figure 2A–C; Supplementary file 1B–D).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the proteomic analysis.

claim: 157 proteins decreased in serum concentration following the 12-week intervention at an FDR below 5%.
source: Of the 3072 proteins quantified, we detected increased serum concentrations of 126 proteins and decreased serum concentrations of 157 proteins following the 12-week intervention at an FDR below 5% (Figure 2A–C; Supplementary file 1B–D).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the proteomic analysis.

claim: 20 proteins increased exclusively in normal weight men.
source: Among these, 20 proteins increased exclusively in normal weight men, whereas 19 proteins increased exclusively in overweight men (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a finding from the group-specific analysis.

claim: 19 proteins increased exclusively in overweight men.
source: Among these, 20 proteins increased exclusively in normal weight men, whereas 19 proteins increased exclusively in overweight men (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a finding from the group-specific analysis.

claim: 4 proteins were uniquely reduced in normal weight men.
source: Four proteins were uniquely reduced in normal weight men, and 66 proteins were uniquely reduced in overweight men (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is a finding from the group-specific analysis.

claim: 66 proteins were uniquely reduced in overweight men.
source: Four proteins were uniquely reduced in normal weight men, and 66 proteins were uniquely reduced in overweight men (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is a finding from the group-specific analysis.

claim: PDGFB and IL7 are both myokines with potential effects on muscle differentiation.
source: For example, platelet-derived growth factor subunit B (PDGFB) and IL7 are both myokines with potential effects on muscle differentiation (Haugen et al., 2010; Hamaguchi et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by citations to Haugen et al., 2010 and Hamaguchi et al., 2023.

claim: FGFBP3 may influence running capacity.
source: Further, fibroblast growth factor-binding protein 3 (FGFBP3) may influence running capacity (Lories et al., 2009) and muscle strength (Casas-Fraile et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Lories et al., 2009.

claim: FGFBP3 may influence muscle strength.
source: Further, fibroblast growth factor-binding protein 3 (FGFBP3) may influence running capacity (Lories et al., 2009) and muscle strength (Casas-Fraile et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Casas-Fraile et al., 2020.

claim: CYB5R2 can preserve skeletal muscle mitochondria function in aging mice.
source: NADH-cytochrome b5 reductase 2 (CYB5R2) can preserve SkM mitochondria function in aging mice (López-Bellón et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to López-Bellón et al., 2022.

claim: FGFBP3 and SWAP70 may protect against weight gain and cardiac hypertrophy, respectively.
source: FGFBP3 and switch-associated protein 70 (SWAP70) may protect against weight gain (Tassi et al., 2018) and cardiac hypertrophy (Qian et al., 2023), respectively.
evidence: Supported by citations to Tassi et al., 2018 and Qian et al., 2023.

claim: DUSP13A is highly specific to skeletal muscle.
source: Finally, dual specificity protein phosphatase 13 isoform A (DUSP13A) is highly specific to SkM (Chen et al., 2004), making it a potential novel muscle-specific marker for long-term exercise.
evidence: Supported by citation to Chen et al., 2004.

claim: A key driver analysis of the 66 proteins identified SLC22A1, a hepatocyte transporter related to liver fat content.
source: A key driver analysis of the 66 proteins identified SLC22A1, a hepatocyte transporter related to liver fat content (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a finding from the key driver analysis shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The 66 proteins displayed a 24% overlap with a known human serum proteomic signature of NAFLD.
source: Furthermore, the 66 proteins also displayed a 24% overlap with a known human serum proteomic signature of NAFLD (Figure 3E; Govaere et al., 2023), but no common proteins with signatures of specific liver cells (The Human Liver Cell Atlas: Aizarani et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a finding from the overlap analysis with the NAFLD signature from Govaere et al., 2023.

claim: Baseline serum protein concentrations in the identified signature of 66 proteins were higher among men with overweight compared to those with normal weight.
source: Baseline serum protein concentrations in the identified signature of 66 proteins were higher among men with overweight compared to those with normal weight, but were reduced or normalized in overweight men following prolonged exercise (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is a finding from the comparison of baseline protein levels between groups shown in Figure 3F.

claim: The first principal component of the 66 proteins correlated positively to liver fat content at baseline.
source: Using principal component analysis of the 66 proteins, the first component correlated positively to liver fat content at baseline (Figure 3G), but not after prolonged exercise (Figure 3H).
evidence: This is a finding from the principal component analysis shown in Figure 3G.

claim: The first principal component of the 66 proteins did not correlate with liver fat content after prolonged exercise.
source: Using principal component analysis of the 66 proteins, the first component correlated positively to liver fat content at baseline (Figure 3G), but not after prolonged exercise (Figure 3H).
evidence: This is a finding from the principal component analysis shown in Figure 3H.

claim: The first principal component of the 66 proteins correlated positively with several liver-related markers at baseline.
source: Similarly, the first component also correlated positively with several liver-related markers at baseline (Figure 3L) and negatively to insulin sensitivity at baseline (Figure 3I), but not after prolonged exercise (Figure 3J).
evidence: This is a finding from the correlation analysis shown in Figure 3L.

claim: The first principal component of the 66 proteins correlated negatively to insulin sensitivity at baseline.
source: Similarly, the first component also correlated positively with several liver-related markers at baseline (Figure 3L) and negatively to insulin sensitivity at baseline (Figure 3I), but not after prolonged exercise (Figure 3J).
evidence: This is a finding from the correlation analysis shown in Figure 3I.

claim: The first principal component of the 66 proteins mediated 37% of the association between baseline insulin sensitivity and liver fat content.
source: The first component mediated 37% of the association between baseline insulin sensitivity and liver fat content (Figure 3K).
evidence: This is a finding from the mediation analysis shown in Figure 3K.

claim: Among the 96 upregulated and 110 down-regulated serum proteins responding to the 12-week exercise intervention, 37 are curated secretory proteins.
source: Among the 96 upregulated and 110 down-egulated serum proteins responding to the 12-week exercise intervention (Figure 2D and E), 37 are curated secretory proteins, and another 46 proteins are predicted as highly likely secretory proteins (Figure 4A–C).
evidence: This is a finding from the secretory protein classification analysis.

claim: 46 proteins are predicted as highly likely secretory proteins among the exercise-responsive proteins.
source: Among the 96 upregulated and 110 down-egulated serum proteins responding to the 12-week exercise intervention (Figure 2D and E), 37 are curated secretory proteins, and another 46 proteins are predicted as highly likely secretory proteins (Figure 4A–C).
evidence: This is a finding from the secretory protein classification analysis.

claim: COL1A1 was the most responsive skeletal muscle mRNA that also had a corresponding increase in serum COL1A1 after prolonged exercise.
source: COL1A1 was the most responsive SkM mRNA that also had a corresponding increase in serum COL1A1 after prolonged exercise (Figure 4D and E).
evidence: This is a finding from the multi-tissue analysis shown in Figure 4D and E.

claim: CCL3 was the most responsive subcutaneous white adipose tissue mRNA that also had a corresponding decrease in serum after prolonged exercise.
source: CCL3 was the most responsive ScWAT mRNA that also had a corresponding decrease in serum after prolonged exercise (Figure 4F and G).
evidence: This is a finding from the multi-tissue analysis shown in Figure 4F and G.

claim: SMOC1 is a known hepatokine with effects on insulin sensitivity in mice.
source: SMOC1 is a known hepatokine with effects on insulin sensitivity in mice (Montgomery et al., 2020), but probably with no causal link to insulin sensitivity in humans (Montgomery et al., 2020; Ghodsian et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to Montgomery et al., 2020 and Ghodsian et al., 2021.

claim: CD300LG displayed increased concentration in serum (+20%, p<0.001) following the 12-week exercise intervention.
source: CD300LG displayed increased concentration in serum (+20%, p<0.001) together with increased levels in both SkM (+60%, p<0.001) and scWAT (+13%, p=0.01) mRNA following the 12-week exercise intervention (Figure 5A–C).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the CD300LG analysis shown in Figure 5A-C.

claim: CD300LG mRNA levels increased in skeletal muscle (+60%, p<0.001) following the 12-week exercise intervention.
source: CD300LG displayed increased concentration in serum (+20%, p<0.001) together with increased levels in both SkM (+60%, p<0.001) and scWAT (+13%, p=0.01) mRNA following the 12-week exercise intervention (Figure 5A–C).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the CD300LG analysis shown in Figure 5A-C.

claim: CD300LG mRNA levels increased in subcutaneous white adipose tissue (+13%, p=0.01) following the 12-week exercise intervention.
source: CD300LG displayed increased concentration in serum (+20%, p<0.001) together with increased levels in both SkM (+60%, p<0.001) and scWAT (+13%, p=0.01) mRNA following the 12-week exercise intervention (Figure 5A–C).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the CD300LG analysis shown in Figure 5A-C.

claim: Changes in serum CD300LG correlated positively with changes in insulin sensitivity after the intervention (rho = 0.59, p=0.002).
source: Changes in serum CD300LG correlated positively with changes in insulin sensitivity after the intervention (rho = 0.59, p=0.002; Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a finding from the correlation analysis shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Serum CD300LG concentration was lower in overweight than normal weight men (–51%, p=0.014).
source: In addition, serum CD300LG concentration was lower in overweight than normal weight men (–51%, p=0.014) and positively correlated with insulin sensitivity before as well as after the 12-week intervention (pretrained: r = 0.50, p=0.001, and post-trained: r = 0.43, p=0.028).
evidence: This is a finding from the comparison between groups.

claim: Serum CD300LG positively correlated with insulin sensitivity before the intervention (r = 0.50, p=0.001).
source: In addition, serum CD300LG concentration was lower in overweight than normal weight men (–51%, p=0.014) and positively correlated with insulin sensitivity before as well as after the 12-week intervention (pretrained: r = 0.50, p=0.001, and post-trained: r = 0.43, p=0.028).
evidence: This is a finding from the correlation analysis.

claim: Serum CD300LG positively correlated with insulin sensitivity after the intervention (r = 0.43, p=0.028).
source: In addition, serum CD300LG concentration was lower in overweight than normal weight men (–51%, p=0.014) and positively correlated with insulin sensitivity before as well as after the 12-week intervention (pretrained: r = 0.50, p=0.001, and post-trained: r = 0.43, p=0.028).
evidence: This is a finding from the correlation analysis.

claim: The change in serum CD300LG concentrations correlated with changes in expression of genes involved in oxidative phosphorylation in both subcutaneous white adipose tissue and skeletal muscle.
source: Pathway analyses revealed that the change in serum CD300LG concentrations correlated with changes in expression of genes involved in oxidative phosphorylation, G2M check point and hypoxia both in ScWAT and SkM (Figure 5E and F).
evidence: This is a finding from the pathway analysis shown in Figure 5E and F.

claim: Serum CD300LG levels showed the strongest enrichment with angiogenesis pathways in subcutaneous white adipose tissue.
source: In ScWAT, serum CD300LG levels also showed the strongest enrichment with angiogenesis pathways (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is a finding from the pathway enrichment analysis shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The change in subcutaneous white adipose tissue CD300LG mRNA levels correlated positively with the change in subcutaneous white adipose tissue mRNA of genes related to angiogenesis/vasculature development.
source: In ScWAT, the change in ScWAT CD300LG mRNA levels correlated positively with the change in ScWAT mRNA of genes related to angiogenesis/vasculature development (Figure 5G).
evidence: This is a finding from the correlation analysis shown in Figure 5G.

claim: 60% of the mRNAs in the angiogenesis pathway correlated with CD300LG in skeletal muscle.
source: For example, 60% of the mRNAs in the angiogenesis pathway correlated with CD300LG (Figure 5H).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the pathway analysis shown in Figure 5H.

claim: CD300LG is highly expressed in adipose tissue compared to other tissues.
source: CD300LG is highly expressed in adipose tissue compared to other tissues (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A), supporting our observation that ScWAT expression was substantially higher than in SkM (Figure 5B and C).
evidence: This is a finding from the human tissue panel analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: CD300LG mRNA in subcutaneous white adipose tissue was primarily expressed in venular endothelial cells.
source: CD300LG mRNA in ScWAT was primarily expressed in venular endothelial cells, but not adipocytes or other cell types present in ScWAT (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B–E).
evidence: This is a finding from the single-cell RNA sequencing analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B-E.

claim: In men, subcutaneous white adipose tissue CD300LG correlated strongly with subcutaneous white adipose tissue, skeletal muscle, and aortic gene expression.
source: In men, ScWAT CD300LG correlated strongly with ScWAT, SkM, and aortic gene expression (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the GD-CAT database analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: The top network of gene expression in subcutaneous white adipose tissue related to subcutaneous white adipose tissue CD300LG mRNA was angiogenesis in men.
source: Consistent with our observations in the MyoGlu exercise intervention study, the top network of gene expression in ScWAT related to ScWAT CD300LG mRNA was angiogenesis (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is a finding from the GD-CAT database analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Skeletal muscle CD300LG correlated strongly with subcutaneous white adipose tissue, skeletal muscle, and aortic gene expression in men.
source: Like ScWAT, SkM CD300LG also correlated strongly with ScWAT, SkM, and aortic gene expression (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is a finding from the GD-CAT database analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The proteasome complex was the top network of gene expression related to skeletal muscle CD300LG mRNA in men.
source: The proteasome complex was the top network of gene expression related to SkM CD300LG mRNA (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is a finding from the GD-CAT database analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2B.

claim: In women, running the same analyses did not reveal associations between CD300LG and angiogenesis.
source: In contrast, running the same analyses in women did not reveal associations between CD300LG and angiogenesis (Figure 5—figure supplement 3A and B).
evidence: This is a finding from the GD-CAT database analysis in women shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3A and B.

claim: Serum CD300LG levels were positively associated with several measures of physical activity in the UK Biobank.
source: Serum CD300LG levels were positively associated with several measures of physical activity (all metabolic equivalent tasks, results from the international physical activity questionnaire and meeting the recommended amount of weekly physical activity or not; Table 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the UK Biobank analysis shown in Table 1.

claim: Serum CD300LG levels were most strongly related to vigorous activity in the UK Biobank.
source: Interestingly, serum CD300LG levels were most strongly related to vigorous activity (Table 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the UK Biobank analysis shown in Table 1.

claim: Serum CD300LG levels were positively associated with fat mass and fat free mass in the UK Biobank.
source: Serum CD300LG levels were also positively associated with fat mass and fat free mass, and negatively associated with glucometabolic traits, including serum glucose levels, Hb1Ac, and the risk of having type 2 diabetes (Table 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the UK Biobank analysis shown in Table 1.

claim: Serum CD300LG levels were negatively associated with serum glucose levels, HbA1c, and the risk of having type 2 diabetes in the UK Biobank.
source: Serum CD300LG levels were also positively associated with fat mass and fat free mass, and negatively associated with glucometabolic traits, including serum glucose levels, Hb1Ac, and the risk of having type 2 diabetes (Table 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the UK Biobank analysis shown in Table 1.

claim: GWAS analyses of CD300LG levels detected 43 independent genome-wide significant genetic associations across the genome.
source: GWAS analyses of CD300LG levels detected 43 independent genome-wide significant genetic associations across the genome (Figure 5—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a finding from the GWAS analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 4.

claim: The most significant SNPs from the CD300LG GWAS lay along chromosome 17, mapping to the genomic region encoding the CD300LG gene.
source: The most significant SNPs lay along chromosome 17, with these SNPs mapping to the genomic region encoding the CD300LG gene (Figure 5—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a finding from the GWAS analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 4.

claim: The MR PRESSO analysis showed a significant negative effect of CD300LG on fasting glucose after outlier correction.
source: Due to the heterogeneity in our results, we therefore performed MR PRESSO to account for outliers. The MR PRESSO analysis showed a significant negative effect of CD300LG on all outcomes (Table 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the MR PRESSO analysis shown in Table 2.

claim: The MR PRESSO analysis showed a significant negative effect of CD300LG on 2 hr post OGTT glucose after outlier correction.
source: Due to the heterogeneity in our results, we therefore performed MR PRESSO to account for outliers. The MR PRESSO analysis showed a significant negative effect of CD300LG on all outcomes (Table 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the MR PRESSO analysis shown in Table 2.

claim: The MR PRESSO analysis showed a significant negative effect of CD300LG on HbA1c after outlier correction.
source: Due to the heterogeneity in our results, we therefore performed MR PRESSO to account for outliers. The MR PRESSO analysis showed a significant negative effect of CD300LG on all outcomes (Table 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the MR PRESSO analysis shown in Table 2.

claim: There is a 51% homology between human CD300LG and mouse Cd300lg.
source: There is a 51% homology between human CD300LG and mouse Cd300lg (Takatsu et al., 2006), and also in mice, Cd300lg is predominantly expressed in adipose tissue endothelial cells (Emont et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to Takatsu et al., 2006.

claim: In mice, Cd300lg is predominantly expressed in adipose tissue endothelial cells.
source: There is a 51% homology between human CD300LG and mouse Cd300lg (Takatsu et al., 2006), and also in mice, Cd300lg is predominantly expressed in adipose tissue endothelial cells (Emont et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to Emont et al., 2022.

claim: Cd300lg levels in subcutaneous white adipose tissue from mice were increased after exercise for 8 weeks (~30% in both female [p=0.03] and male [p=0.01] mice).
source: In MoTrPAC (Sanford et al., 2020), Cd300lg levels in scWAT from n = 12–15 male and female mice were increased after exercise for 8 weeks (~30% in both female [p=0.03] and male [p=0.01] mice) (Figure 5—figure supplement 6A–C).
evidence: This is a finding from the MoTrPAC mouse exercise model shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 6A-C.

claim: Male mutants for the Cd300lgtm1a(KOMP)Wtsi allele displayed impaired glucose tolerance.
source: Based on data from n = 3050 mice from PhenoMouse male, but not female, mutants for the Cd300lgtm1a(KOMP)Wtsi allele displayed impaired glucose tolerance (Figure 5—figure supplement 6D), but no change in fasting glucose and insulin (Figure 5—figure supplement 6E and F).
evidence: This is a finding from the PhenoMouse knockout model shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 6D.

claim: Female mutants for the Cd300lgtm1a(KOMP)Wtsi allele did not display impaired glucose tolerance.
source: Based on data from n = 3050 mice from PhenoMouse male, but not female, mutants for the Cd300lgtm1a(KOMP)Wtsi allele displayed impaired glucose tolerance (Figure 5—figure supplement 6D), but no change in fasting glucose and insulin (Figure 5—figure supplement 6E and F).
evidence: This is a finding from the PhenoMouse knockout model shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 6D.

claim: Mutant male mice for the Cd300lgtm1a(KOMP)Wtsi allele displayed increased lean mass.
source: Mutant male, but not female, mice also displayed increased lean mass (Figure 5—figure supplement 6G) and less fat mass (Figure 5—figure supplement 6H).
evidence: This is a finding from the PhenoMouse knockout model shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 6G.

claim: Mutant male mice for the Cd300lgtm1a(KOMP)Wtsi allele displayed less fat mass.
source: Mutant male, but not female, mice also displayed increased lean mass (Figure 5—figure supplement 6G) and less fat mass (Figure 5—figure supplement 6H).
evidence: This is a finding from the PhenoMouse knockout model shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 6H.

claim: A larger number of serum proteins responded to the 12-week exercise intervention in overweight men than in normal weight men.
source: In response to the 12-week exercise intervention, a larger number of serum proteins responded in overweight men than in normal weight men (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: This is a finding from the comparison of protein responses between groups shown in Figure 2B and C.

claim: SLC22A1 regulates the hepatic glucose fatty acid cycle affecting gluconeogenesis and lipid metabolism.
source: This was related to SLC22A1, which regulates the hepatic glucose fatty acid cycle affecting gluconeogenesis and lipid metabolism (Liang et al., 2018), and may influence liver fat accumulation (Chen et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to Liang et al., 2018 and Chen et al., 2014.

claim: SLC22A1 may influence liver fat accumulation.
source: This was related to SLC22A1, which regulates the hepatic glucose fatty acid cycle affecting gluconeogenesis and lipid metabolism (Liang et al., 2018), and may influence liver fat accumulation (Chen et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Chen et al., 2014.

claim: COL1A1 is a collagen peptide that is related to muscle damage, turnover, and extracellular matrix remodeling in response to exercise.
source: However, COL1A1 is a collagen peptide that is related to muscle damage, turnover, and extracellular matrix remodeling in response to exercise (Jacob et al., 2022) and may mostly reflect muscle restructuring and not represent signaling effects to distant tissues.
evidence: Supported by citation to Jacob et al., 2022.

claim: CCL3 is a monocyte chemoattractant protein that may be related to immune cell infiltration in adipose tissue.
source: CCL3 is a monocyte chemoattractant protein that may be related to immune cell infiltration in adipose tissue (Barry et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Barry et al., 2017.

claim: CD300LG is a cell surface protein with a transmembrane domain, but is also a predicted secretory protein.
source: CD300LG is a cell surface protein with a transmembrane domain, but is also a predicted secretory protein (Meinken et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Meinken et al., 2015.

claim: CD300LG is expressed in endothelial cells.
source: Furthermore, the exact link between CD300LG and glucose metabolism is not clear, but possibly related to the fact that CD300LG is expressed in endothelial cells (Umemoto et al., 2013), linked to blood pressure (Støy et al., 2014), lymphocyte binding (Umemoto et al., 2006), blood triacylglycerol levels (Surakka et al., 2015; Støy et al., 2015), and molecular traffic across the capillary endothelium (Takatsu et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citation to Umemoto et al., 2013.

claim: CD300LG is linked to blood pressure.
